page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Margin notes stand in the left margin, beside the lines of the text. Page number and running head at the top.

main_text.p: cham crearent ; deinde virum aliquem insignem eligerent quem secum Presbyterum constituerent loco ejus qui factus est Patriarcha, ut ita semper extarent duodecim. Neque desiit Alexandriæ institutum hoc de Presbyteris, ut scilicet Patriarchas crearent ex Presbyteris duodecim, usque ad tempora Alexandri Patriarchæ Alexandrini, qui fuit ex numero illo trecentorum & octodecim (id est ex Patribus Nicænæ Synodi an. D. 325. sub Constantino celebratæ) post hæc observat præstantissimus Dallæus Eutychium de summâ rei cum Hieronymo consentire, de tempore leviter discrepare. Vindiciarum Auctor negat levem esse Hieronymum inter & Eutychium discrepantiam; Verùm quæcunque sit illa dissonantia, nec Viri docti caufam juvare, nec Dallæi hypothesi nocere potest: in eo quippè conveniunt Hieronymus & Eutychius, quod utérque narret Alexandriæ Presbyteros per longum temporis spatium Episcopos sibi creare esse solitos, quod adversâ fronte pugnat cum Ignatianis placitis, juxta quæ nihil sine Episcopo fieri debet; nec mihi arridet Viri docti cavillatio, dicentis Hieronymum solam Presbyteris Episcopi nominationem concedere, non item electionem nec ordinationem, quasi ab aliis electo & or[?]Pearf.
Note: the left-margin references in the printed text read "Pearf. cap. 10. pag. 163. 164.165.", placed beside the lines "Hieronymum inter", "pantiam", "fonantia" and "nec Dallæi".

page.notes: The final word is cut off at the foot of the page and continues on the next page; read as "or[?]" (probably "ordinato"). The printed margin references are placed beside lines: "Pearf." beside "Hieronymum inter", "cap. 10." beside "pantiam", "pag. 163." beside "fonantia", "164.165." beside "nec Dallæi". Doubtful italic/roman boundaries in the first lines. Ligature "ct" in "docti" printed as ɛ-form, transcribed as "docti". Printed "ejus" and "electo" left as printed. The first-line fragment "cham" is a fragment from the previous page.
